questions.q:
The exterior angle of a regular polygon is 30°.
(a) Find the number of sides of the polygon. [1]
(b) Find the sum of the interior angles of the polygon. [1]
questions.tip: Exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°.

questions.q:
In triangle ABC, AB = AC and angle BAC = 48°.
Find angle ABC. Give a geometrical reason for your answer.
ms: B1: base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal (and angles in a triangle add up to 180°)
questions.model:
Angle ABC = (180 − 48) ÷ 2 = 66°.
Reason: base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, and angles in a triangle add up to 180°.
questions.tip: Name the property: 'isosceles triangle' earns the reason mark, 'because AB = AC' alone does not.

questions.q:
AB is parallel to CD. A straight line crosses AB at P and CD at Q.
Angle APQ = (3x + 10)° and angle PQD = (5x − 30)°. These two angles are alternate angles.
(a) Find the value of x. [2]
(b) Find angle PQC. Give a geometrical reason for your answer. [2]
ms: (b) B1: angles on a straight line add up to 180° (with angle PQD = 70°)
questions.model:
(a) Alternate angles are equal: 3x + 10 = 5x − 30 → 40 = 2x → x = 20.
(b) Angle PQD = 5(20) − 30 = 70°.
Angle PQC = 180 − 70 = 110° (angles on a straight line add up to 180°).
questions.tip: Write 'alternate angles are equal', never 'Z angles'.

questions.q:
(a) Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 4 times its exterior angle. Find the number of sides of the polygon. [3]
(b) A regular pentagon and a regular hexagon share one side. Find the angle between them at one end of the shared side (the angle outside both shapes). [1]
ms: (a) M1: exterior angle 36°, or 360 ÷ their exterior angle
questions.model:
(a) Interior + exterior = 180°, so e + 4e = 180 → e = 36°. Number of sides = 360 ÷ 36 = 10.
(b) Pentagon interior angle = 108°, hexagon interior angle = 120°.
Angles at a point: 360 − 108 − 120 = 132°.
questions.tip: The interior and exterior angle of any polygon lie on a straight line, so they add up to 180°.

questions.q:
A, B, C and D are points on a circle, in that order. AC is a diameter of the circle.
Angle BAC = 28° and angle CAD = 35°.
(a) Find angle ABC. Give a geometrical reason. [2]
(b) Find angle BDC. Give a geometrical reason. [2]
(c) Find angle BCD. [2]
ms: (b) B1: angles in the same segment are equal
(c) M1: angle BCA = 62° or angle ACD = 55° (or uses opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral with angle BAD = 63°)
questions.model:
(a) Angle ABC = 90° (angle in a semicircle).
(b) Angle BDC = angle BAC = 28° (angles in the same segment are equal).
(c) Triangle ABC: angle BCA = 180 − 90 − 28 = 62°.
Triangle ACD: angle ADC = 90° (angle in a semicircle), so angle ACD = 180 − 90 − 35 = 55°.
Angle BCD = 62 + 55 = 117°.
(Check: angle BAD = 28 + 35 = 63° and 63 + 117 = 180°, opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral.)
questions.tip: Look for the arc each angle 'stands on'; angles standing on the same arc are equal.

questions.q:
TA is a tangent to a circle, centre O, at the point A. B and C are points on the circle, with C on the major arc AB.
Angle TAB = 58°.
(a) Find angle ACB. Give a geometrical reason. [2]
(b) Find angle AOB. Give a geometrical reason. [2]
(c) Find angle OAB. Give a geometrical reason. [2]
ms: (b) B1: angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
(c) B1: tangent is perpendicular to the radius (90 − 58), or base angles of isosceles triangle OAB since OA = OB (radii)
questions.model:
(a) Angle ACB = 58° (alternate segment theorem).
(b) Angle AOB = 2 × 58 = 116° (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference).
(c) OA = OB (radii), so triangle OAB is isosceles: angle OAB = (180 − 116) ÷ 2 = 32°.
Or: angle OAT = 90° (tangent perpendicular to radius), so angle OAB = 90 − 58 = 32°.
questions.tip: Learn the exact wording of each circle theorem; 'alternate segment theorem' is the accepted phrase.
